document.title: SITREP 6: Pakistan/Afghanistan Reaction to U.S. Strikes (Islama 06433)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Confidential] SITREP on reactions to the 20 Aug strikes. Gen. Joseph Ralston was in Islamabad during the strikes, and Pakistani officials were outraged at the airspace violation. The Taliban called the Khost strikes appalling and hardened their stance on extraditing bin Laden. Mullahs Zakiri and Shinwari issued a fatwa requiring Muslims to protect bin Laden. Excised.

mentions.quote: TALIBAN LEADER: MULLAH OMAR CLAIMED IN AN INTERVIEW EARLIER IN THE DAY THAT THE U.S. HAD OFFERED TO TALK WITH THE TALIBAN
OMAR WAS UPSET WITH BIN LADIN FOR CONTINUING TO MAKE THREATS AGAINST THE U.S. WHILE IN AFGHANISTAN

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: Leader of terrorist network targeted by U.S. strikes; guest of Taliban in Afghanistan

mentions.quote: BIN LADIN HAD GIVEN MULLAH OMAR ASSURANCES THAT HE WILL LISTEN TO THE TALIBAN LEADERSHIP
AUGUST 20 U.S. STRIKES ON THE TERRORIST NETWORK OF USAMA BIN LADEN
MULLAH OMAR ASSISTANT MAULAWI WAKIL AHMED, WHO HE INTERVIEWED ON AUGUST 24
WAKIL AHMED SAID THE TALIBAN WILL NOT HAND OVER BIN LADIN TO ANYONE

persons.name: Rahimullah Yusufzai
persons.role: Journalist with close connections to the Taliban (reporting for The News)

mentions.quote: RAHIMULLAH YUSUFZAI, A JOURNALIST WITH CLOSE CONNECTIONS TO THE TALIBAN, REPORTED IN AUGUST 25 "THE NEWS"
ALLEGED CONFIRMATION BY FOREIGN MINISTER SARTAJ AZIZ, SPEAKING IN THE SENATE, THAT AN UNEXPLODED CRUISE MISSILE HAD BEEN FOUND
FORMER PM BENAZIR BHUTTO CALLED FOR AN INVESTIGATION OF THE USE OF PAKISTANI SOIL BY THE U.S.

persons.name: Joseph Ralston
persons.role: Vice Chairman, U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff

mentions.quote: VC JCS GEN RALSTON WAS IN ISLAMABAD "HAND HOLDING" KEY PAKISTANI OFFICALS DURING THE STRIKES

persons.name: Zakiri
persons.role: Key Taliban religious leader reportedly issuing fatwa to protect Bin Ladin

mentions.quote: TALIBAN RELIGIOUS LEADERS, INCLUDING KEY MULLAHS ZAKIRI AND SHINWARI, HAD RECENTLY ISSUED A "FATWA"

persons.name: Shinwari
persons.role: Key Taliban religious leader reportedly issuing fatwa to protect Bin Ladin

mentions.quote: KEY MULLAHS ZAKIRI AND SHINWARI, HAD RECENTLY ISSUED A "FATWA" REQUIRING MUSLIMS TO PROTECT BIN LADIN
CLASSIFIED BY ALAN BASTHAM, CHARGE D'AFFAIRES.

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Hosts Bin Ladin; said it would not hand him over but would try him if solid evidence presented; Khost stringers held.

organizations.name: al-Qa'ida
organizations.notes: Referred to as the terrorist network of Usama bin Ladin; camps in Khost struck 20 Aug 1998.

organizations.name: Harakat-ul-Mujahideen
organizations.notes: Kashmiri terrorist group that sponsored a demonstration of several hundred in Lahore.

organizations.name: Afghan Islamic Press
organizations.notes: Reported Omar's claim of U.S. talks offer.

organizations.name: Government of Pakistan
organizations.notes: Accused by opposition of failing to detect or assisting U.S. strike.

places.name: Khost
places.significance: Location of terrorist camps struck 20 Aug 1998; stringers detained there 21 Aug.

places.name: Shatingar
places.significance: Place where unexploded cruise missile reportedly found.

events.description: U.S. cruise missile strikes on Bin Ladin terrorist camps in Khost.
Four Pakistani/Afghan stringers reportedly held by Taliban on entering Khost.
Yusufzai reports Omar upset with Bin Ladin's threats; interviews Wakil Ahmed.
Mullah Omar claims U.S. offered talks after strikes.
Planned demonstration in Islamabad by mullahs and students.
Taliban religious leaders including Mullahs Zakiri and Shinwari issued a fatwa requiring Muslims to protect bin Ladin.
Taliban held four Pakistani and Afghan stringers for international wire services who entered Khost Province; equipment reportedly smashed; later reportedly freed.
Embassy Islamabad sent SITREP 6 on Pakistan/Afghanistan reaction to U.S. strikes.
U.S. cruise missile strikes on terrorist camps in Khost targeting bin Ladin's network.
Sartaj Aziz in the Senate reportedly confirmed an unexploded cruise missile found at Shatingar, Baluchistan; Pakistan to protest at UN.
Harakat-ul-Mujahideen sponsored a demonstration of several hundred people in Lahore.
Consulate Peshawar American staff temporarily withdrawn to Islamabad due to threat information.
Planned demonstration in Islamabad by some mullahs and Islamic students.
Mullah Omar claimed in an interview that the U.S. offered talks after the strikes, adding nothing is left to talk about after the missile raid.
Yusufzai interviewed Wakil Ahmed; also published a story that Omar was upset with bin Ladin.
Embassy POLOFF met a well-known former resistance leader with close links to the Taliban, who criticized the strikes.

relationships.quote: THE STRIKES HAVE ANGERED MANY IN THE TALIBAN MOVEMENT WHO CONSIDERED THEMSELVES FRIENDS OF THE U.S.

relationships.quote: VC JCS GEN RALSTON WAS IN ISLAMABAD "HAND HOLDING" KEY PAKISTANI OFFICALS DURING THE STRIKES

relationships.quote: THE NEWS ALSO CARRIES A SHORT FRONT-PAGE PIECE, DATELINE WASHINGTON, STATING THAT VC JCS GEN RALSTON WAS IN ISLAMABAD

relationships.quote: THE U.S. WAS ALWAYS OPEN TO TALK WITH THE AFGHAN FACTIONS, INCLUDING THE TALIBAN.

key_claims: Mullah Omar claimed the U.S. offered talks after the 20 Aug 1998 strikes but said nothing was left to discuss after the missile raid.
Yusufzai reported Omar was upset that Bin Ladin kept threatening the U.S. and feared he was positioning himself as alternate leader.
Taliban spokesman Wakil Ahmed said they would not hand over Bin Ladin but would try him if solid evidence was presented.
Taliban clerics Zakiri and Shinwari reportedly issued a fatwa requiring Muslims to protect Bin Ladin.
A former resistance leader with Taliban links said the strikes angered pro-U.S. Taliban and hardened Taliban positions.
Harkat-ul-Mujahideen held a Lahore demonstration; the Embassy withdrew Peshawar staff due to threats.
